source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation
finding: Writing intermediate steps to a scratchpad lets models do multi-step computation they fail at directly. This is the clearest machine analogue of an epistemic action: the written steps do work the model cannot do in one pass.
numbers: Polynomial evaluation, 137B few-shot: direct 8.8% vs scratchpad 20.1%; 8B fine-tuned 31.8% vs 50.7%. Python execution few-shot 11% vs 26.5%, fine-tuned 20% vs 41.5%. Addition 1-8 digits: no-scratchpad models fail even at the largest size, scratchpad models succeed past a critical size. 9-10 digit out-of-distribution: no-scratchpad fails completely, scratchpad improves with size.
limits: Small synthetic tasks, few-shot or fine-tuned; scratchpad format was hand designed. Few-shot execution scratchpad condition slightly modified (starred in paper).
agent_relevance: S2/S4: let the agent write intermediate state in a fixed trace format.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Writing reasoning steps before the answer lifts accuracy a lot, but only at large scale.
numbers: PaLM 540B: GSM8K standard 17.9% vs CoT 56.9% (+39.0); SVAMP 69.4 vs 79.0; ASDiv 72.1 vs 73.9; AQuA 25.2 vs 35.8; MAWPS 79.2 vs 93.3.
limits: Gains appear mainly at very large scale; arithmetic slips remain because the model itself computes.
agent_relevance: Text steps are a weak epistemic action; prefer actions that move computation outside the model.

source: Gao et al. (2022) PAL: Program-aided Language Models
finding: The model writes code and an interpreter runs it. Offloading computation beats written reasoning, and the gap grows with large numbers.
numbers: Codex GSM8K: CoT 65.6% vs PAL 72.0%; PAL with majority vote 80.4%. GSM-Hard (larger numbers): CoT 23.1% vs PAL 61.2%. On Colored Objects, CoT accuracy drops as object count rises while PAL stays near 100%. 16 of 25 manually checked CoT thoughts were identical on GSM8K and GSM-Hard, so bigger numbers break arithmetic, not the plan.
limits: Needs a code-trained model; problem must be expressible as code.
agent_relevance: S4: model plans, code computes. Epistemic action = take load off the model's weakest part.

source: Chen et al. (2022) Program of Thoughts Prompting
finding: Separating reasoning (model) from computation (interpreter) beats CoT on math and finance QA. A calculator patch on CoT is not enough.
numbers: Few-shot PoT over CoT: more than 8% on GSM8K, AQuA, TabMWP; 4% on SVAMP; about 20% on FinQA and ConvFinQA; 8% on TATQA. Averages: about 8% math word problems, 15% financial; zero-shot about 12%. PoT+self-consistency beats CoT+SC by about 10%. CoT+calculator gives only mild gains. Of 198 PoT failures: 47% value grounding, 33% logic, 15% both, 5% other.
limits: AQuA algebra still only 58%. With K=2 exemplars, variance up to 7%.
agent_relevance: Errors move from arithmetic to grounding values; have code check that values came from the problem.

source: Li et al. (2023) Chain of Code: Reasoning with a Language Model-Augmented Code Emulator
finding: Running code where it runs and letting the model emulate the lines that cannot run beats CoT and pure code on BIG-Bench Hard.
numbers: BBH average, text-davinci-003, single task: Direct 55, CoT 72, CoC 84 (human average 68). PaLM 2-S: 49, 61, 78. Cross-task: 50, 55, 61 and 45, 47, 47. Ablations single task: Python only 48 (-36), LM-state only 63 (-21), LM only 57 (-27).
limits: Cross-task prompting gains are small for PaLM 2-S (+2 over direct). Needs an interpreter in the loop.
agent_relevance: The external action need not be exact; hybrid run-or-simulate is a usable S4 fallback.

source: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
finding: Interleaving acting (search, lookup) with a reasoning trace beats acting alone on interactive tasks. Acting without thoughts loses track of state.
numbers: ALFWorld: best ReAct 71% vs best Act 45% vs BUTLER 37%; worst ReAct trial 48% beats both best; mean relative gain over Act 62%. WebShop: +10 points absolute over best prior. HotpotQA EM (PaLM 540B): Standard 28.7, CoT 29.4, Act 25.7, ReAct 27.4, best combination 35.1. FEVER: 57.1, 56.3, 58.9, 60.9, best 64.6.
limits: On HotpotQA plain ReAct (27.4) is below CoT (29.4); gains come from combining with CoT-SC. Failures from uninformative search results.
agent_relevance: Pair every external look-up with a written reading of what came back; fall back to internal reasoning when the tool returns nothing.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: A verbal reflection written to memory after a failed trial improves the next trial, using real environment feedback.
numbers: Over strong baselines: +22% ALFWorld (134 environments), +20% HotpotQA, +11% HumanEval; HumanEval 91% pass@1 vs GPT-4 80%. ReAct-only ALFWorld gains halt between trials 6 and 7. Reflection triggers when the same action and response repeat for more than 3 cycles or over 30 actions are taken.
limits: Relies on an external success signal such as unit tests or an environment flag.
agent_relevance: Written notes after real outcomes act as external memory. Trigger on a signal (G1).

source: Huang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Self-review with no external feedback does not help and often hurts. Earlier gains used oracle labels to decide when to stop.
numbers: GPT-3.5 over two rounds: GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7; CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 to 41.8; HotpotQA 26.0 to 25.0 to 25.0. GPT-4: GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; CSQA 82.0 to 79.5 to 80.0; HotpotQA 49.0 to 49.0 to 43.0.
limits: Intrinsic setting only; GPT-4 runs on 200-question samples (100 for HotpotQA).
agent_relevance: Re-reading your own text is not epistemic action. Supports G2: revise only from real output.

source: Schick et al. (2023) Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
finding: A 6.7B model that learned when to call a calculator beats much larger models on math word problems zero-shot.
numbers: ASDiv/SVAMP/MAWPS: GPT-J 7.5/5.2/9.9; Toolformer with tools disabled 14.8/6.3/15.0; Toolformer 40.4/29.4/44.0; OPT 66B 6.0/4.9/7.9. The model calls the calculator on 97.9% of examples.
limits: Table was extracted from PDF text with interleaved rows; assignment by row order, check the paper before quoting.
agent_relevance: A call rule can be fixed by the scaffold rather than learned.

source: Liu et al. (2022) Mind's Eye: Grounded Language Model Reasoning through Simulation
finding: Running a physics engine (MuJoCo) and feeding the result back is an epistemic action. It lifts physics reasoning and lets small models match big ones.
numbers: UTOPIA, 39 tasks: GPT-3 175B vanilla 24% zero-shot, 38.2% few-shot. Mind's Eye: +27.9% zero-shot and +46.0% few-shot absolute (abstract); text elsewhere says 18.4% and 34.2%. GPT-3 Babbage 1.3B with Mind's Eye 29.8% zero-shot vs vanilla GPT-3 175B 29%.
limits: Two different gain figures appear in the same paper. Narrow domain, rule-based text-to-simulation.
agent_relevance: Split experimenting from reasoning: the world gives ground truth, the model reasons.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Visual Sketchpad: Sketching as a Visual Chain of Thought
finding: Letting a multimodal model draw and look at its own drawing raises accuracy in math and vision. Closest direct test of 'sketch to think' in a model.
numbers: Average gain 11.2% (GPT-4o) and 23.4% (GPT-4 Turbo) on geometry, graph, function and game tasks. Max flow GPT-4o 66.3% (+41.3). Convexity and parity: Turbo above 90%, 4o above 88%. Game strategy +3 to 10. V* Bench 80.3% (+18.5 Turbo, +14.3 4o). BLINK average +6.6 (Turbo), +9.0 (4o). Relative depth +12.1 (4o) vs +2.4 (Turbo). Abstract: +12.7% math, +8.6% vision. Versus other frameworks Sketchpad is the only one improving all tasks; SoM can hurt; Visprog is below base on every task.
limits: Stronger model gains more. Tool errors propagate. Needs detection and depth modules for vision tasks.
agent_relevance: Supports a sketch step in S4, but the model must read its own drawing well.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Visualization-of-Thought Elicits Spatial Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Asking a text model to draw ASCII grids of its state at each step helps spatial tasks, but the drawn state is often wrong.
numbers: GPT-4: natural-language navigation VoT 59.0 vs CoT 54.0 vs no-viz 35.5 (VoT beats no-viz by 23.5; p<0.16 vs CoT). Visual tiling VoT 63.94 vs CoT 54.15 vs no-viz 49.62. Route planning completion 40.77 vs 37.17. State tracking rate 87.1% (VoT) vs 57.4% (CoT) in tiling. Visualization accuracy only 24-26%; correct move in 65-77% of cases when drawing was accurate. On a clock-ring task CoT 52.5% beat VoT 49.5% (200 items). Prompt 'use ascii-art to visualize' raised tracking by 78.5 to 98.5% and task by 3.5 to 62.5%.
limits: Table was extracted with interleaved rows; assigned by row order. 2D grid worlds only; small models benefit unevenly.
agent_relevance: Drawn state helps only when correct: keep a code-side grid and check the model's sketch against it.

source: Pfau, Merrill, Bowman (2024) Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformer Language Models
finding: Meaningless filler tokens can replace CoT on some parallel tasks, but only after dense training. So some of the benefit of extra tokens is raw computation, not content.
numbers: Llama 34M: 3SUM 100% with filler, 2SUM-Transform 94%, both fail without filler. Gap grows with input length up to 12. Commercial LLMs show no filler benefit in earlier tests. Stays within TC0.
limits: Synthetic tasks; learning needs parallelizable demonstrations; no transfer to natural CoT.
agent_relevance: Contrast case: filler gives compute but no information. Our scaffold should use real external state.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
finding: Written reasoning is often not what the answer depends on. Filler tokens do not help; reliance on the chain varies by task.
numbers: Filler tokens (' ...'): no accuracy increase at any length. Paraphrasing the CoT left accuracy near the original on almost all tasks. Truncation and mistake-adding tests show tasks range from answering unchanged under 10% of the time to over 60%; AQuA shows low reliance; larger models give less faithful reasoning.
limits: One model family; per-task table values not all recorded.
agent_relevance: The model's own text is not a record of its reasoning (SCHEMA section 1). Epistemic value comes from verifiable outputs.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Position: Agent Should Invoke External Tools ONLY When Epistemically Necessary
finding: Position paper (v4, May 2026). Defines epistemic necessity: use a tool only when the task cannot be done reliably by internal reasoning on the current context. Over-delegation is also a failure.
numbers: No experiments or scores. Introduces Theory of Agent; names overthinking and overacting as miscalibrated internal-versus-external decisions.
limits: Normative; no measured effect. Abstract page only read for this one (full text not read).
agent_relevance: Rule for S2/S4: act externally on a signal that internal reasoning is unreliable, not by default.

source: Fu et al. (2026) Beyond Solution-Centric Search: Adaptive Inquiry and Knowledge Revision for Autonomous ML Engineering (Iris)
finding: An agent loop splitting actions into interventional (change the solution) and epistemic (probe unknowns, leave the solution unchanged). Removing epistemic actions cost accuracy.
numbers: MLE-Bench 75 tasks: any-medal 64.9% (12 h). Ablation on 15 small tasks, 6 h, one run each: Full Med+ 80.0, any-medal 66.7, gold 20.0. Without epistemic actions: Med+ 73.3, any-medal 60.0 (-6.7), gold 20.0. Without adaptive topology: any-medal 40.0. Without information management: any-medal 53.3, gold 13.3. Cross-domain: 3-Banking 30.3 vs Claude Code 26.3; BrowseComp 67.7 vs 57.5; HumanEval 47.0 vs 41.5; GSM8K 68.4 vs 54.0.
limits: One run per task, 15 tasks: a 6.7 point change is one task. Term not tied to Kirsh and Maglio in the text I read.
agent_relevance: Direct 2026 use of the term in an agent loop. Trigger: epistemic action when current evidence cannot separate the next steps. Evidence of benefit is thin.

source: Liu (2026) Track, Rank, Crack: Epistemic Working Memory Scales Multi-Hop Reasoning in Language Agents (SLEUTH), memory structure
finding: A structured external working memory (confirmed facts, ranked hypotheses, open questions) improves multi-hop QA agents. Unstructured notes do not reliably help.
numbers: Claude Sonnet 4.6, 20 turns, EM: HotpotQA SLEUTH 66.1 vs Reflexion 61.4 (+4.7), ReAct 60.2. MuSiQue 4-hop ReAct 42.0; gain +11.1 to +11.9 across hops. 2Wiki ReAct 73.1. Ablation 4-hop: Facts only 49.9 (+7.9 over ReAct); Facts+Hypotheses 48.9; Facts+Questions 47.7; full triple adds +3.2. Unstructured Notes: inconsistent. Token overhead 42% (HotpotQA) to 29% (4-hop).
limits: Single author; 70% nudge point tuned on same benchmarks; models Sonnet 4.6 and GLM-5 only.
agent_relevance: Keep typed state, not a diary (S2).

source: Liu (2026) SLEUTH, commitment trigger and protocol adherence
finding: A late commitment nudge works only when structured state exists, and a weaker model follows the structure only when the harness enforces it.
numbers: 4-hop MuSiQue Sonnet: SLEUTH EM 49.1 to 53.1 with nudge at turn 14 (70% of budget); ReAct plus same nudge 42.2 (+0.2). Without nudge SLEUTH timeout 24.7%, and 92% of timed-out runs held the gold answer; conditional accuracy 64.6 vs ReAct 51.1. Nudge@6 48.1, @10 51.4, @14 52.8. GLM-5 protocol adherence 15% to 99% with adapted prompt plus runtime check; 4-hop 29.9 to 48.9 (+19.0), beating Sonnet unstructured ReAct 42.0.
limits: Same single-paper caveats.
agent_relevance: Code should enforce the state format and trigger commit on a counted budget fraction (program decides).

source: Feng et al. (2024) Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems
finding: Theory: constant-depth transformers without CoT are limited (AC0 at constant precision, TC0 otherwise). With T CoT steps they can compute what circuits of size T compute.
numbers: No benchmark scores. Experiments on arithmetic, permutation composition and circuit value problems show CoT needed especially for low-depth transformers.
limits: Expressivity result, not a measure of prompted behaviour.
agent_relevance: Formal reason written steps help: each token is extra serial computation held outside the weights.

source: Chae et al. (2024) Language Models as Compilers: Simulating Pseudocode Execution Improves Algorithmic Reasoning (Think-and-Execute)
finding: Writing task-level pseudocode once, then simulating its execution per instance, beats zero-shot CoT and per-instance code on algorithmic tasks.
numbers: Seven algorithmic tasks. Zero-shot CoT beats direct by 11.1% average with GPT-3.5-Turbo. Think-and-Execute beats CoT and has about 2x the average score of Chain-of-Code in their Table 3. Task-level pseudocode 60.4% vs human-written pseudocode 55.7% on a subset.
limits: Author list inferred; per-task tables not copied. The 2x claim is against their rerun of CoC.
agent_relevance: Write the algorithm first as an artefact, then execute step by step (S2).

source: Gap note 2026-10-26: no LLM replication of the Kirsh and Maglio Tetris finding located
finding: Web search quota ran out. arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs rate-limited. No paper testing an LLM on rotate-to-see or on the epistemic versus pragmatic split itself was found. The closest machine uses are Iris and SLEUTH (2026).
numbers: None. The one successful web search returned no source mapping Kirsh and Maglio onto scratchpad or tool use.
limits: Absence from a limited search, not proof of absence. Not opened.
agent_relevance: Treat 'LLM agents show human-like epistemic action' as untested; only the functional analogues (external trace, code, sketch) are measured.

source: Aytes et al. (2025) Sketch-of-Thought: Efficient LLM Reasoning with Adaptive Cognitive-Inspired Sketching
finding: Short, structured 'sketch' reasoning (symbols, chunks) keeps accuracy while cutting output tokens. The external trace does not need to be long prose.
numbers: Token reduction up to 84% vs CoT across 15 datasets. Qwen-2.5-32B: 82.30% vs CoT 82.24% with 74.36% fewer tokens. Commonsense: 92.00% at 34 tokens vs CoT 91.48% at 177 tokens.
limits: Read from abstract and results text only in part; per-dataset tables not recorded. Paradigm chosen per question by a router.
agent_relevance: S2 notes can be terse and typed; length is not the active ingredient.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Visual Sketchpad, tool-use behaviour
finding: Models pick sketch tools in task-appropriate ways, much as people search an image: detection, sliding window and zoom for small objects, depth estimation for depth questions.
numbers: GPT-4o uses vision specialists more often than GPT-4 Turbo; on semantic correspondence GPT-4o uses segmentation on 40% of tasks. Visprog (program-composed tools) scored below the base model on all single-image tasks tested.
limits: Describes behaviour, not a causal test of why the sketch helps.
agent_relevance: Let the model choose among a small fixed set of epistemic tools, and test each tool alone.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring Faithfulness in CoT, post-hoc reasoning
finding: Truncating the chain shows that on some tasks the model already has its answer before it writes the reasoning, so the writing is not doing the work there.
numbers: Models give the same answer without the full CoT under 10% of the time on the least post-hoc tasks and over 60% on the most post-hoc; AQuA shows low reliance (accuracy drop -4.69% when CoT removed in one test).
limits: One model; one prompt format.
agent_relevance: Only count a written step as epistemic if removing it changes the result; test by ablating the trace.

source: Huang et al. (2023) with Shinn et al. (2023): the feedback source decides
finding: The same reflect-and-retry loop gains with real external feedback and loses without it.
numbers: Reflexion with unit tests or environment signal: +11% HumanEval (91% pass@1), +22% ALFWorld. Intrinsic self-correction GPT-4 on GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 and HotpotQA 49.0 to 43.0 after two rounds.
limits: Different tasks; comparison is by reading, not a controlled test.
agent_relevance: Define epistemic action in the schema as an action that returns information from outside the model's own generation.
